claims.claim: The 2-anilinopyrimidine kinase inhibitor structure in C14 has an absolute oral bioavailability of 46% after a single 180 mg oral dose in healthy volunteers, well above the 20% threshold.

The same 2-anilinopyrimidine scaffold in C04 and C15 achieved absolute oral bioavailability of 77% in the fed state and 57% in the fasted state in healthy volunteers, showing that this chemotype with a basic piperazine and high polar surface area can exceed 20%.

The query is a pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidinone 2-anilino derivative with a piperazinyl-aniline solubilizing group, closely analogous to the high-bioavailability 2-anilinopyrimidine kinase inhibitors; the physicochemical low-absorption prior is not affirmative evidence of F < 20%.
No transferable record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for this chemotype; the only near-threshold record (tacrolimus, ~20-25%) is a structurally unrelated macrolide.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability record for the query molecule itself is present in the supplied cards.
Transfer from the 2-anilinopyrimidine analogs is structural rather than a same-molecule measurement; formulation, dose, and food effects may differ.
No query-specific human IV/oral AUC comparison, solubility, or permeability data are supplied.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high: F >= 20% is better supported. Although the physicochemical prior is low, multiple structurally analogous 2-anilinopyrimidine kinase inhibitors with similar ionization and polar-surface-area liabilities show absolute oral bioavailability of 46-77%, all above threshold, and no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%.
